findings.title: TSMC Form 6-K: Statement Regarding the Unauthorized Access of Employee Personal Data
findings.summary_md: TSMC stated that some current and former employee data was made available on an external website without authorization. The company said it found no evidence that TSMC systems were compromised and that the exposed information matched data stored in a cloud service provider's systems, unrelated to company operations or customer data. TSMC said it was informing impacted personnel and providing support, and had engaged the cloud vendor, relevant investigating authorities, and a third-party cybersecurity agency.

findings.title: TSMC Investigates Third-Party Cloud Breach Affecting Employee Data
findings.summary_md: ICO Optics reported that TSMC filed an SEC Form 6-K addressing an external data security incident in which personal details of a subset of current and former employees appeared on an external website without authorization. The leaked records closely matched information stored in an independent cloud service vendor's systems, and TSMC initiated notification and support for affected personnel. A joint investigation involving the cloud vendor, cybersecurity experts, and legal authorities was underway.

findings.title: TSMC says employee personal data was posted online from a cloud provider's systems
findings.summary_md: MLQ.ai reported that TSMC said on November 12 that personal data on some current and former employees was posted on an external website without authorization, in an SEC statement signed by CFO Wendell Huang. The data matches information stored in a cloud service provider's systems, and TSMC said it found no evidence its own systems were compromised and that operations and customer data were not involved. TSMC did not give a record count; Wccftech, citing Taiwanese press reports, said the files cover about 46,000 employee records and that the hackers demanded 3 bitcoin.
